title: The Labyrinth
subtitle: PROCEDURAL MAZES · SEARCH · COLLECTION
description: Guide the fire through 12 connected mazes. Find the glowing ring in each maze to open the next one.
explanation: Each maze is generated with an iterative depth-first search that carves passages through a grid. A breadth-first search then finds the farthest reachable tile and places the ring there. Hold W/A/S/D or the arrow keys to move. The movement system checks the next tile against the walkable grid, so the fire slides along walls instead of passing through them. Collecting a ring advances to the next deterministic maze. Collect all 12 rings to finish.
algorithm: DFS carves a connected maze → BFS finds a far tile → collision-aware movement → collect ring → next maze
learning_goals: Describe how depth-first search carves passages using a stack of visited cells.
Explain breadth-first search and why it finds a farthest reachable ring location here.
Follow how grid coordinates, collision checks, and level progression fit together.
review_points: How does the generator avoid visiting a cell twice?
Which data structure represents pending DFS work, and what does popping it mean?
How does BFS ensure the chosen ring tile is reachable?
Where is the boundary between maze data and the systems that move the hero?
practice_tasks: Change the maze seed and observe which layouts change while connectivity remains.
Change the grid size, then inspect the start tile, ring tile, and wall boundaries.
Temporarily place the ring on a random tile and observe why the BFS placement is safer.
Trace one ring collection from input, through the collision grid, to the next maze.
